issue.title: aws_athena_capacity_reservation target_dpus validation minimum should be 4, not 24
issue.body:
### Terraform and AWS Provider Version ```console Terraform v1.5.7 on darwin_arm64 + provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws v6.49.0 Your version of Terraform is out of date! The latest version is 1.15.5. You can update by downloading from https://www.terraform.io/downloads.html ``` ### Affected Resource(s) or Data Source(s) aws_athena_capacity_reservation ### Expected Behavior The resource should accept target_dpus = 4, as AWS updated the minimum capacity for Athena Capacity Reservations to 4 DPUs on February 10, 2026. ### Actual Behavior The provider validation rejects target_dpus = 4 with the error: Error: Invalid Attribute Value Attribute target_dpus value must be at least 24, got: 4 The validation is hardcoded to >= 24, which no longer matches the AWS API. ### Relevant Error/Panic Output ```console │ Error: Invalid Attribute Value │ │ with aws_athena_capacity_reservation.AthenaCapacityReservation, │ on main.tf line 17, in resource "aws_athena_capacity_reservation" "AthenaCapacityReservation": │ 17: target_dpus = 4 │ │ Attribute target_dpus value must be at least 24, got: 4 ``` ### Sample Terraform Configuration
Click to expand configuration ```hcl resource "aws_athena_capacity_reservation" "example" { name = "example" target_dpus = 4 } ```
### Steps to Reproduce 1. Define an aws_athena_capacity_reservation resource with target_dpus = 4 2. Run terraform plan 3. Provider validation fails before any API call is made ### Debug Logging
Click to expand log output ```console n/a — the error is a provider-side validation failure, no API call is made ```
### GenAI / LLM Assisted Development n/a ### Important Facts and References AWS announced 4 DPU minimum support on February 10, 2026: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/02/amazon-athena-one-minute-capacity-reservations The AWS console (Create capacity reservation page) also shows "Minimum: 4 DPU". The fix is to update the target_dpus validation in the provider from >= 24 to >= 4. ### Would you like to implement a fix? No
issue.author: Aya-Schechner
